research_question: Given the exact same frozen mechanism-first plan, can an explicit semantic-preservation translation contract reduce plan-to-CodeQL translation loss and generic-template collapse compared with the original M1 translation while retaining compilability?
answer_to_research_question: NO IMPROVEMENT OBSERVED IN THIS CWE-639 TRAIN PILOT. T1 preserved the same 0/7 semantic alignment, 7/7 generic-template collapse, and 6/7 translation loss as T0. Matched V3 repair restored full compilation but did not recover semantic alignment or detection.
main_observed_bottleneck: Semantic information represented at the planning stage is not preserved during unification into one CWE-level CodeQL query. Compiler-oriented repair can recover CodeQL executability without recovering the missing security relations or validation semantics.
scientific_boundary: This is a single CWE-639 TRAIN pilot. It does not establish generalization to other CWEs or TEST.
